name: The Disputed Reach

stars.name: Valen's Claim
stars.notes: A stable yellow main-sequence star whose habitable zone is broad enough to support two marginally habitable worlds—the root cause of the territorial dispute that has defined this system for two centuries.

planets.name: Cinder Pact
planets.notes: Tidally locked, sun-scorched rock. The day side is molten slag; the night side is littered with automated sensor arrays monitoring ship traffic entering the system.

planets.name: Contested Ground
planets.notes: Arid but habitable world with scattered settlements from both the Valen Compact and the Dravathi Hegemony. The equatorial zone is a no-man's-land of burnt towns and minefields.

planets.name: Second Claim
planets.notes: A water-rich world with archipelago settlements. The Dravathi hold the northern hemisphere; the Valen Compact holds the south. The ocean between is mined and patrolled ceaselessly.

planets.name: Rubble March
planets.notes: Rocky, airless world used as a staging ground by both factions. Its largest moon, Redoubt, houses hardened bunkers and ammunition depots.

planets.name: Warden Giant
planets.notes: Banded ammonia giant whose extensive moon system provides cover for fleet anchorages. Both factions maintain hidden resupply depots among the outer moons.

planets.name: Far Exile
planets.notes: Distant ice dwarf beyond the conflict zone. Smugglers use its shadow for covert jump calculations away from patrol routes.

anomalies.name: The Scar Line
anomalies.notes: A permanent debris field from the Battle of Second Claim (2691), where 47 warships were destroyed in a single engagement. Navigation through the field requires careful plotting to avoid hull-puncturing wreckage.

asteroid_belts.name: Treaty Belt
asteroid_belts.composition: silicate and metal, mixed with battle debris
asteroid_belts.notes: Natural asteroid belt contaminated with warship wreckage from multiple engagements. Salvage operations are technically illegal under the current armistice but occur constantly.

stations.name: Valen Checkpoint Alpha
stations.notes: Valen Compact's primary command station in-system. Heavily armed and shielded, it serves as both fleet coordination center and political headquarters for the Compact's territorial claims.

stations.name: Dravathi Anchor
stations.notes: Dravathi Hegemony fleet anchorage and troop rotation facility. Its docking arms can service up to twelve capital ships simultaneously.

stations.name: Neutral Observer Platform
stations.notes: Third-party monitoring station operated by the Meridian Accord. Tasked with documenting ceasefire violations. Both factions accuse it of bias.

faction_control.notes: Two habitable worlds, two claimants, no resolution. The Valen Compact asserts historical settlement rights; the Dravathi Hegemony claims conquest rights from the 2687 annexation. The current armistice is eighteen months old and already fraying.

history: Colonized by the Valen Compact in 2541, the system's two habitable worlds attracted rapid settlement. The Dravathi Hegemony invaded in 2687, claiming the system fell within their ancestral expansion corridor, sparking a four-year war.

The Battle of Second Claim in 2691 was the bloodiest single engagement of the conflict, with 47 warships destroyed and over 11,000 spacers killed. Neither side achieved decisive victory, leading to the first of seven armistices.

The current ceasefire, brokered by the Meridian Accord in 2724, partitions both habitable worlds along hemispheric lines. Skirmishes along the equatorial demarcation zone on Contested Ground occur weekly, and intelligence services on both sides prepare for the next escalation.
description: The Disputed Reach is a system defined by what it could have been. A stable yellow star, two habitable worlds, a broad asteroid belt rich in metals—under peaceful circumstances, this system would be a thriving colony. Instead, it is a wound that refuses to close. The inner rocky world bristles with sensors. The two habitable planets are scarred by partition lines and pocked with military installations. The gas giant's moons hide fleet anchorages. Even the asteroid belt is contaminated with the wreckage of warships.

The conflict between the Valen Compact and the Dravathi Hegemony has frozen the system in a state of armed standoff. Contested Ground's equatorial zone is a wasteland of burnt settlements and unexploded ordnance, while Second Claim's ocean is divided by mine-chains and patrol corridors. The Neutral Observer Platform documents violations that neither side acknowledges, and the armistice erodes a little more with each passing month. Military traffic is constant; civilian commerce barely exists.

For opportunists, the Reach offers danger and profit in equal measure. The Treaty Belt's salvage is technically prohibited but practically unguarded. Both factions quietly hire mercenaries and deniable assets for operations they cannot officially sanction. Smugglers who can navigate the mine-seeded ocean of Second Claim command premium rates. And intelligence brokers find the system an inexhaustible source of secrets—every soldier, every station, every patrol route is someone's commodity.
